songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Lovelight and psychedelic Alligator > Caution sequence
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers a scorching Turn On Your Lovelight, a tightly woven Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One sandwich, and an extended Alligator → Caution saga. Jerry Garcia’s lead work is in top form, while Pigpen adds a memorable organ solo on New Potato Caboose. Overall the performance is consistently high‑energy with excellent soundboard capture.
ai_show_review.review: The November 11, 1967 Shrine Exposition Hall show captures the Dead at a pivotal moment of raw, psychedelic vigor. From the opening blaze of Turn On Your Lovelight, where Garcia spins two blistering solos—one described as “splitting the fabric of the universe”—the band rides an electric current that never quits. The set’s centerpiece is the classic Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One → Cryptical Envelopment sandwich, executed with tight transitions and a sense of daring improvisation that feeds directly into a funk‑laden New Potato Caboose, highlighted by Pigpen’s soaring organ solo and Mickey Hart’s glockenspiel accents. The second half builds an all‑out jam marathon: Alligator segues into a thunderous drum break before resurfacing for another round, then morphs seamlessly into Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks), delivering a psychedelic climax that feels both chaotic and perfectly calibrated. Throughout, the rhythm section stays locked in, providing a solid foundation for Garcia’s soaring lead tones and the group’s exploratory spirit.

best_recording.reason: Crisp soundboard capture with clear early set and standout performances of Lovelight, Cryptical Envelopment, The Other One, New Potato Caboose, and Alligator → Caution

key_highlights: Explosive Turn On Your Lovelight with two legendary Garcia solos
Tight Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One sandwich that drives the set forward
Funky New Potato Caboose featuring Pigpen’s organ solo and Mickey’s glockenspiel
Extended Alligator → Caution saga that showcases the band’s psychedelic peak

band_performance.Jerry: Delivers two of his most celebrated Lovelight solos, with a tone described as otherworldly and a left‑ear lead that sounds like an older master.
band_performance.Mickey: Provides steady drumming throughout and adds glockenspiel texture on New Potato Caboose.
